key_insight: FlashVector targets the hidden performance losses in production model serving by optimizing across the full serving stack, not just one layer. Its core idea is that an agent can help coordinate GPU kernels, framework graphs, server behavior, and feature processing to boost throughput and reduce cost.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of improving recommender-system model serving throughput in a deeply layered stack where each layer requires specialized expertise. This cross-layer optimization is hard to do manually and does not scale as workloads grow and change.
method: Uses an agent to reason across multiple layers of the serving stack instead of optimizing each layer in isolation.
Focuses on hierarchical optimization spanning GPU kernels, ML framework computation graphs, model servers, and on-demand feature processing.
Aims to automate expert-level cross-layer decisions that improve throughput and cost efficiency in production serving.
impact: For ML practitioners, this means higher serving efficiency and lower infrastructure cost without requiring deep expertise in every system layer. It also offers a path to keep performance optimization scalable as production workloads evolve.
visual_elements: Layered stack diagram showing GPU, framework, server, and feature processing layers
Before/after throughput or cost comparison chart
Agent workflow diagram illustrating cross-layer optimization decisions
Icons for compute, server, and feature pipeline to emphasize the end-to-end serving path
paper_title: FlashVector: Agent for Hierarchical Model Serving Stack Optimization
paper_authors: Qi Wu, Lohan Lemire, Kai Meng, Zhongmou Cai, Raphael Bargues
